description: A PHP static analysis tool for finding errors and security vulnerabilities in PHP applications

latest_release.body:
<!-- Release notes generated using configuration in .github/release.yml at 9e0d0f88bc0a4233357a9aeb4b32da060644e196 -->

## What's Changed
### Features
* Report the CWE weaknesses of issues, and use the issue type as the SARIF rule id by @danog in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14156
* Remove the taints a value can't carry once it matches an anchored pattern, or a list of words through a string cast by @danog in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14161
* Require the Doctrine plugin, and enable it when composer.json requires Doctrine by @danog in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14165
* Report weak hashes and ciphers, seeded random number generators, insecure cookies and XXE by @danog in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14160
* Make what symfony/yaml parses with PARSE_OBJECT an unserialize sink by @danog in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14172
### Fixes
* [6.x] Fix crash when a class extends a class_alias() declared later by @wleeaf in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12494
* Fix alter ignoring MissingThrowsDocblock suppression by @d-mitrofanov-v in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/11586
* Accept the $flags parameter of ArrayObject/ArrayIterator asort()/ksort() by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14127
* Charge __toString when builtins convert values or array values to strings by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14129
* Taint the dynamic properties of a tainted object by @danog in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14162
* Fix gettype() !== narrowing to a class named after the type by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14152
* Analyse Foo::C and $foo::C with one helper (experimental) by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14153
* Merge NamespaceStatementsDiffer into FileStatementsDiffer (experimental) by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14148
* Analyze methods of another file through one helper keeping the root file by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14147
* Taint what the preg_replace_callback() callback returns by @danog in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14067
* Keep the taints of an array iterated with foreach when it can also be a string by @danog in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14168
* [Experimental] One builder per kind for the assertions of === and !== by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14155
* Fix memory-limit option in psalm-refactor by @Aaqibhafeezkhan in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14070
* Define the offsets before an offset asserted on a list by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14178
* Give conditions built-in assertions only when the call resolves to the built-in function by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14151
* Fix exponential analysis time of a negated in_array() over a literal list inside || by @shu-chen-dot-ca in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14072
* fix(reports): escape control and bidi characters in the human-readable reports by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12804
* fix(taint): link the arguments after the first one a variadic collects to its parameter by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13112
* fix(assertions): @psalm-assert accepts an offset of an argument by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13005
* fix(assert): an assertion on a scalar parameter does not narrow a mixed argument by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13895
* Assert a non-empty string after file_exists, is_file and the other file tests by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12595
* Fix crashes on first-class callables of inherited and provider-confirmed methods by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12124
* Bind the method templates of the parent docblock an untyped override inherits by @shu-chen-dot-ca in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14073
* Fix master CI: keep declared assertions of a call compared strictly to false by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14191
* Fi

detail.readme:
Psalm

[![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/v/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/dt/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm coverage](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/coverage.svg?)](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm level](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/level.svg?)](https://psalm.dev/) Psalm is a static analysis tool for finding errors in PHP applications. [Join the official Psalm news channel](https://t.me/psalmphp) and the Psalm community on [Telegram](https://t.me/psalmphp_community) and [Discord](https://discord.gg/RwH8rEpxt9)! ## Installation To get started, check out the [installation guide](docs/running_psalm/installation.md). ## Live Demo You can play around with Psalm [on its website](https://psalm.dev/). ## Documentation Documentation is available on [Psalm’s website](https://psalm.dev/docs), generated from the [docs](https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/blob/master/docs) folder. ## Support Psalm development You can support Psalm development by requesting a support contract from [Daniil Gentili](https://daniil.it), the only active maintainer of Psalm. Support contracts can cover full integration of Psalm into existing codebases, support for Psalm issues and development of additional Psalm features. See [here »](https://daniil.it) for info, pricing and contact information. ## Interested in contributing? Have a look at [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Who made this Built by Matt Brown ([@muglug](https://github.com/muglug)). Maintained by Daniil Gentili ([@danog](https://github.com/danog)), Alies Lapatsin ([@alies-dev](https://github.com/alies-dev)) and Orklah ([@orklah](https://github.com/orklah)). Former maintainer: Bruce Weirdan ([@weirdan](https://github.com/weirdan)). The engineering team at [Vimeo](https://github.com/vimeo) have provided a lot encouragement, especially [@nbeliard](https://github.com/nbeliard), [@erunion](https://github.com/erunion) and [@nickyr](https://github.com/nickyr).
